items.title: Johnny St. Cyr Interview, 1958-08-27
items.q: Pop Foster, he and I bought a method at the same time. He bought a bass method. It was 1918, when we got in St. Louis.

ctx.x: Then you still didn't get a regular method to start on, I guess?

No, I didn't get a guitar method, I just got a music method. I first got a piano catechism. Yeah. And I learned the notes there, and how to build chords, first, third and fifth. I worked them out on the guitar. And then I bought a guitar method. George, George, Pop Foster, he and I bought a method at the same time. He bought a bass method. It was 1918, when we got in St. Louis. He bought a bass method, and I bought a guitar method. And we went to work on them.
Who was it? You telling us that other guys in the band would be running around at night, but you always...

items.title: Johnny St. Cyr Interview, 1958-08-27
items.q: He was the clarinet player in the Olympia band when they first started... I think he went back to the Imperial with Manuel.

ctx.x: Yes, I remember when Joe Brooks was with him.

Well, nobody much in all this trip is hardly mentioned, Piku. Do you remember when did you hear him? Well, wait a minute, wait a minute. Nobody's been talking about him lately, like Pops Foster, nobody has mentioned him.

He was the clarinet player in the Olympia band when they first started. Oh, yeah. Yeah, he got bigger and a little bit later. I think he went back to the Imperial with Manuel. He was the clarinet player with the Olympia band when they first organized it. And later on he left the band and went with the Imperial. And then George, George Baquet, no, the big guy Louis, went with the Olympia. Then he went with the superiors, and George Baquet went with the Olympia.
